archetypes.name: bash-portability
archetypes.rationale: The release-prepare.sh loop uses piped-grep and herestring IFS parsing in ways that need Bash 3.2 compatibility verification, and the BASH_AUTHORING.md wrapped-grep trap risk applies to the while-read loop body.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the new `while IFS= read -r commit_line` loop in `.claude/skills/release/scripts/release-prepare.sh` for BASH_AUTHORING.md compliance: check whether any `grep` call inside or after the loop is a bare top-level grep (not piped or command-prefixed), whether `$'\t'` and `<<<` herestrings are bash 3.2–compatible, and whether `[[ " $written_pr_numbers " == *" ${api_num} "* ]]` dedup correctly handles leading/trailing whitespace edge cases or numeric-string collisions. Also verify the fake-git `case` branch `"--format=%H %s"` in `test-release-prepare.sh` is exercised correctly when the script passes the format as a single quoted argument. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: pointer-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: The new implement pointer (write on bootstrap, clear on Step 18) has no teardown in the crash/error path, and the double _assert_no_symlink call in write_implement_env_main and missing atomic-replace for plain files may leave stale or partial state.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the lifecycle of the implement session pointer introduced in `python/session_env.py` (`write_implement_env_main`, `clear_implement_pointer_main`) and its call sites in `scripts/implement-bootstrap.sh` (write) and `skills/implement/SKILL.md` Step 18 (clear). Verify that the pointer is cleared on all exit paths including error branches, Step 18 timeouts, and runs that skip Step 18 entirely. Check whether `_atomic_write` for a regular file (not a symlink) correctly replaces an existing pointer without a TOCTOU window, and whether calling `_assert_no_symlink_path_or_ancestors` twice in `write_implement_env_main` (before and after `mkdir -p`) provides the intended guarantee or creates an unnecessary double check. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: ci-inprogress-block
archetypes.rationale: _wait_for_ci_ready with CI_MONITOR_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT=3600 introduces a blocking wait of up to 1 hour inside evaluate_failure, which changes the outer loop's stall behavior and interacts with the existing transient-rerun and fix-attempt logic.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the new `_wait_for_ci_ready` function in `python/ci_monitor.py` and its integration into `evaluate_failure`. Verify that the 3600-second default in `config.CI_MONITOR_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT` is intentional and will not cause the outer ship-pr loop to stall for an entire hour on a briefly-in-progress run. Check whether `blind_rerun_attempted` and `upfront_ready_stash` logic is still correct after the new early-return path for an in-progress state that exhausts the timeout, and whether the `clock` parameter threaded into `evaluate_failure` is forwarded correctly to `_wait_for_ci_ready` in all call sites. Also verify that `collect_failed_logs` called inside the poll loop does not have side effects that accumulate across iterations. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
